prompt: A chat app must show new messages to the recipient within 100 ms, without the client polling.
why: Keep a persistent connection so the server pushes messages instantly.
trap: A queue moves messages between services, but the last hop to the phone needs a push channel.

prompt: A sports app shows live scores that change every few seconds to a million connected fans.
why: Push updates over open connections (WebSockets or server-sent events).
trap: Polling a CDN every second multiplies requests and still lags.

prompt: In a shared whiteboard, everyone should see others' cursors move in real time.
tells: see others' cursors move in real time
why: A bidirectional connection streams small updates both ways with minimal latency.
trap: Event logs help with history, but live cursors need low-latency push.

prompt: Riders watch their driver's car move on the map until pickup, updating every second.
why: Push location updates down an open connection.
trap: A geo index finds nearby drivers; tracking one known driver is a push problem.
